draft.title: Staying safe in floods and storms
card: People can lower their risk in floods and storms by preparing early and making safe choices during the event.
Plan and kit
An emergency plan says where to go and who to contact. An emergency kit holds items such as a torch, a radio, batteries, water and first aid supplies.
Floodwater
Never drive, walk or ride through floodwater. It can hide damage to the road and can be deeper and faster than it looks.
SES
The State Emergency Service (SES) helps people in floods and storms. People should follow its advice, such as when to leave.
draft.remember: Plan and pack ahead, stay out of floodwater, and follow the SES.

a.q: Why should a driver never drive through floodwater?
opts: It can hide road damage and be deeper than it looks
It always makes the car's engine stop at once
It is only unsafe when the water is brown
It is only unsafe at night
a.why: Floodwater can hide damage to the road and can be deeper and faster than it looks. The wrong options add conditions such as colour or night time, but floodwater is a risk in any conditions.
a.clue: Think about what the driver cannot see under the water.

b.q: A storm is heading for Tom's town and the power may go out. Which item is best to have in his emergency kit?
opts: A battery radio and spare batteries
A board game and a pack of cards
A set of new school books
A bicycle pump and a helmet
b.why: A battery radio lets Tom hear warnings and advice if the power fails. The board game and cards may pass time but do not help keep him informed or safe.
b.clue: Which item still works with no power and brings news?

a.best: It can hide road damage and be deeper than it looks

b.best: A battery radio and spare batteries

problems.detail: Every wrong option uses an absolute ('always', 'only'), while the right option is the only one hedged with 'can', as the card is. A student could pick it by ruling out the absolutes without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The facts are accurate and both answers are clear. In question a, every wrong option uses 'always' or 'only' and the right one is the only option with 'can', so the answer can be guessed without knowing the idea.

a.q: After heavy rain, Mia's dad sees water flowing over the road ahead. What is the safest choice?
opts: Turn back and take a different, dry route
Drive through slowly if it looks shallow
Walk in first to check how deep it is
Drive through fast to get across quickly
a.why: Floodwater can hide damage to the road and can be deeper and faster than it looks, so nobody should drive, walk or ride through it. Driving slowly through water that looks shallow is tempting, but you cannot tell its real depth or what is under it.
a.clue: Can you trust how deep the water looks?
